title: Lighthouse Systems — Quickstart & Time-to-First-Token Discovery
summary: Intro discovery covering Redwood quickstart, free credit trial, and realistic path to first token. Customer wants a low-friction hosted start but has enterprise constraints (data residency, KMS, audit logs) and asked about Dedicated/Private when they scale. Agreed next steps: trial invites, security pack, and a short pilot to validate latency and cost per token on their sample workload.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
Performance expectations and KV cache / batching
next_steps: Jordan to send trial invite + quickstart links and sample prompts (by 2025-11-21)
Priya to provision a mini benchmark run and share a spreadsheet template for latency/cost metrics (by 2025-11-25)
Maya to share sample prompt set and PII sensitivity notes (by 2025-11-22)
Schedule 45m follow-up pilot review in 2 weeks (tentative 2025-12-04)
Jordan to attach SOC2 and network diagram to the thread
action_items: Jordan Miles - create trial account + invite Lighthouse engineers (due 2025-11-21)
Priya Anand - run 10k token benchmark on hosted small model and share results + cost breakdown (due 2025-11-25)
Maya Ruiz - supply sample prompt set and expected qps/latency SLOs (due 2025-11-22)
Samir Kahn - confirm allowed egress IPs and whether they need VPC peering for Private (due 2025-11-24)
transcript: Header: Date: 2025-11-20 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Evan, Maya, Samir (Lighthouse)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we want to walk through the self-serve quickstart, how you get to first token, and then talk about longer term options if needed

[00:18] Evan (Lighthouse): yep thanks. high level: we're evaluating a hosted start to move fast, but we have to check data residency and key mgmt. we also want to understand costs for production at scale
[00:34] Priya (Redwood): awesome — we'll cover both. quick question, what's your initial workload? chat assistant or document search?
[00:45] Maya (Lighthouse): mostly internal docs QA and a small customer support assistant. initial qps low, spikey, and we care about sub-300ms token latency for UX in some paths
[00:58] Samir (Lighthouse): and from infra side, we need to know whether Redwood can do VPC peering or on prem later. currently we run everything in GCP europe-west1

[01:10] Jordan (Redwood): totally. for quickstart we normally recommend hosted API — sign up, use SDK or curl, drop tokens. time-to-first-token is usually <30 mins if you have an OpenAPI prompt set — we'll send a quickstart with examples
[01:30] Evan: good. what about free credits? how long do they last and are they per-account or per org?

[01:38] Jordan: free credits are applied to your organization account, usually 30 days. for PLG trial we give a starter credit tier — i'll include exact amounts in the email, but you can get to first token without touching any billing info
[01:52] Priya: note, some customers hit limits around model concurrency; we can raise them for pilot. Also be aware of continuous batching and kv cache behavior — that affects latency/cost tradeoffs
[02:10] Maya: kv cache? i've heard it called K V cash in a previous transcript, can you clarify?
[02:14] Priya: sorry, that's kv cache — it's the key/value cache for autoregressive decoding, helps when you have repeated prefixes. reduces repeated compute and cost
[02:28] Samir: on the security side, we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, and ability to rotate keys via our KMS — are those supported in hosted?

[02:40] Jordan: hosted supports SSO and you can bring your own KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and an integration path with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. i'll attach SOC2 and the network diagram
[02:55] Evan: and data residency? we have EU customer data that must stay in EU. do you have region controls?
[03:03] Priya: yes, we have region routing for hosted and Dedicated pools can be reserved in europe regions. Private can be fully on-prem or VPC-restricted for strict residency
[03:20] Jordan: quick note: 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes referenced as Redwood Dedi in notes — it's the reserved GPU pools with SLA and predictable throughput, cost is different than hosted.

[03:37] Maya: let's talk about pilot success criteria. i think we want: 1) get first token from hosted with our prompts, 2) measure 95th pctl latency under expected qps, 3) measure cost/token baseline
[03:52] Priya: that matches what we recommend. we can run a 1-week pilot on hosted with the free credits and provision higher concurrency to emulate spikes
[04:08] Evan: how do you handle fallback if a hosted region is saturated? do you have automated fallback to cheaper models or other regions?

[04:18] Jordan: we do smart routing — policy-based routing to region or compatible model variants, plus canary rollouts. for customer-critical paths we suggest Dedicated or Private eventually for guaranteed throughput
[04:32] Samir: any known gotchas for initial integration? like prompt-engineering or tokenization surprises?
[04:40] Priya: tokenization can vary by model; we'll share a snippet to estimate token counts locally. also watch for long context windows and alignment of system prompts — they'll affect cost
[04:57] Maya: do you have SDKs for Node and Python? we prefer Python currently
[05:02] Jordan: yes, SDKs for Node/Python and simple curl examples. we'll add a sample repo link in the follow-up
[05:10] Evan: curious about observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces. is that in the console?
[05:18] Priya: yes, Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. retention windows are configurable depending on your plan
[05:30] Samir: for the trial, will we get access to the console?
[05:33] Jordan: yes, trial orgs get console access with limited retention. for Dedicated customers you get longer retention and extra observability features as an add-on
[05:45] Evan: pricing question — if i start hosted and later want Dedicated, how does migration work? do we re-pin model versions?

[05:54] Priya: migration is straightforward — same API surface, you point to a new endpoint or route policy. you can pin model versions and rollback if needed. cost model changes because Dedicated is reserved capacity
[06:08] Maya: what about quantization / reduced precision options — do you support quantized model variants to reduce cost?
[06:15] Priya: yes, we advise on quantization profiles via Redwood Optimize; for pilot we'll recommend safe quantization levels and run quality checks against your eval prompts

[06:30] Jordan: quick aside — customers sometimes ask about competitors. a couple of teams try in-house serving or the big APIs like OpenAI; the differentiator we try to show is the production tooling and predictable economics
[06:48] Evan: ok. for next steps i want to confirm we get trial creds and a one-pager on security + an expected timeline for pilot
[06:55] Jordan: check — i'll send trial + security pack. Priya will run an initial benchmark using your prompt set once Maya drops it in the shared doc
[07:06] Maya: i'll upload prompts later today. also note some prompts contain customer-identifying tokens; we need to redact or we can run in Private later
[07:18] Samir: do you keep logs of full payloads in hosted? we need to know retention and ability to purge
[07:25] Priya: hosted keeps audit logs and request traces; retention is plan-dependent. for strict requirements we recommend Private where you control log persistence and can use your KMS
[07:40] Jordan: okay let's recap quickly — deliver trial, attach SOC2 & network diagram, Priya to run bench and share template, Maya to post prompts. follow-up in ~2 weeks
[07:55] Evan: sounds good. any blockers from our side? i don't think so, just internal scheduling and Samir will check networking constraints
[08:05] Samir: yes i'll verify whether we can allow outbound to hosted endpoints or if we need VPC peering. will get back by Monday
[08:15] Jordan: perfect. quick practical: expect an invite to the trial console within 24 hours and a separate email with security docs
[08:25] Maya: one more thing — do you have a recommended prompt-caching pattern? we have a lot of repeated system prompts
[08:33] Priya: yes, prefix caching plus KV cache reuse is typical. we can share an implementation note. that reduces cost on repeated contexts
[08:45] Evan: and benchmarks — what's a realistic cost/token for the smaller models?
[08:50] Priya: depends on model and quantization; we'll provide a ballpark in the follow-up and then refine after the 10k token run
[09:00] Jordan: any legal/procurement concerns now or later?
[09:03] Evan: later — but we will need terms for Dedicated if we move there. procurement usually asks for SLA and liability terms
[09:12] Jordan: we can surface the enterprise package details if needed. ok, last check — timeline? are you aiming for a POC before end of year?
[09:20] Maya: yes, we'd like to validate basic metrics this month and present to ops for a Q1 Dedicated eval
[09:28] Jordan: great. i'll put a tentative follow-up on 2025-12-04. thanks everyone
[09:35] Evan: thanks — talk soon
[52:00] Call end
